Who We Are

Since 1954, Cupertino Electric, Inc. (CEI) has been powered by people who’ve built a reputation for delivering high-profile, complex projects. Real, tangible things that alter the landscape and improve lives. And we've done it with integrity for more than 70 years. We’re problem solvers and innovation seekers. We’re team players and safety fanatics. And we're proud to be part of Quanta Services (PWR:NYSE), North America's largest employer of skilled craft labor. Because what we do is important, but how we do it is everything.

THE PURCHASING TEAM

The purchasing team manages all equipment and materials purchases for both job sites and corporate expenditures. This includes vetting vendors and establishing and maintaining relationships with new and loyal suppliers

About The Role

The Procurement Data Analyst is responsible for maintaining the accuracy, integrity, and effectiveness of procurement and asset-related data to support operational efficiency and informed business decisions. This role serves as a key steward of procurement master data, including item master records, equipment and fleet data, vendor pricing, and procurement system information. The position analyzes data trends, develops reports and dashboards, supports vendor pricing and point-of-sale data management, and collaborates with cross-functional teams to improve processes, enhance system capabilities, and support automation initiatives. Working with general direction, the Procurement Data Analyst independently manages assigned data domains, investigates issues, recommends solutions, and collaborates with stakeholders to implement improvements.

Serve as a steward of procurement master data, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency across key datasets, including the Item Master, equipment and fleet data, vendor pricing, and procurement systems.
Maintain the Item Master throughout its lifecycle, including new item creation, standardization, updates, and data cleanup to support consistent use across the organization.
Analyze procurement and asset-related data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement, supporting process optimization and informed decision-making.
Coordinate vendor pricing updates, including weekly pricing maintenance and the collection of monthly or quarterly point-of-sale (POS) data, ensuring timely and accurate data availability.
Partner with cross-functional teams to improve data quality, streamline processes, enhance system functionality, and support automation initiatives. Conduct analyses of equipment categories and project mobilizations to support buy-versus-rent decisions.
Develop and maintain reports and dashboards that track procurement metrics, supplier performance, and system effectiveness, ensuring insights are accurate, actionable, and aligned with business objectives.
Partner with procurement leadership and IT teams in evaluating and implementing system enhancements and automation opportunities that improve efficiency and data integrity.
Independently manage assigned responsibilities, exercising sound judgment to identify issues, evaluate alternatives, recommend solutions, and drive issues through resolution.
Participate in testing, validation, and implementation of system enhancements and updates, working with cross-functional teams to ensure successful deployment and minimal operational disruption.
Create and maintain documentation for data structures, business processes, reporting, and system procedures to promote standardization and knowledge sharing.

About You

Knowledge of master data management principles, and supply chain data concepts, including item master, vendor, pricing, and asset/equipment data.
Knowledge of data governance practices, data quality standards, and methods for maintaining accurate and consistent business data.
Skill in analyzing and interpreting procurement, asset, and operational data to identify trends, issues, and opportunities for improvement.
Skill in developing reports, dashboards, and performance metrics using reporting and data visualization tools.
Skill in using enterprise systems and databases (e.g., ERP, procurement, inventory, or asset management systems) to maintain and analyze data.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate recurring data maintenance activities, and meet established deadlines with a high degree of accuracy.
Ability to collaborate effectively with procurement, operations, finance, IT, suppliers, and other stakeholders to resolve data and process issues.
Ability to identify root causes of data discrepancies, evaluate solutions, and make sound recommendations based on analysis.
Ability to document business processes, data standards, and system procedures to support consistency, compliance, and knowledge sharing.
Ability to support system enhancements, testing activities, and process improvement initiatives through effective communication, organization, and attention to detail.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities as well as possession of any required licenses or certifications is qualifying.

Education:
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related field.

Licensure/Certifications: N/A

Experience:

Three (3) or more years of experience in data analytics, business systems, master data management, business analysis, process improvement, or a related function.

Experience with Microsoft Power Platform strongly preferred, including Power BI, Power Query, Power Automate, Power Apps, and Dataverse, with hands-on experience developing, maintaining, or troubleshooting reporting, workflows, applications, or automation solutions.

Experience working with enterprise systems and business data, including ERP, asset management, procurement, inventory, or similar platforms, is preferred.

Experience with JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, procurement, construction, or other asset-heavy environments is a plus.

Who We Are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all. We are searching for a Senior Data Analyst, Operations Workforce Strategy to join the Aurora Data Solutions team, who would be based in San Francisco, CA. In this role, you will forecast, allocate, and optimize all operations headcount to align resource plans and schedules to hiring and vendor engagement strategies. You will be at the forefront of our staffing and vendor management strategy, working closely with cross-functional teams to gather and analyze data, identify trends, and develop plans that support our operational goals. This role requires strategic orchestration, analyzing workforce needs, and driving momentum under a fast-paced, ever-changing environment.

Partner with Operations, Strategy, Recruiting, and Finance leaders to forecast and align headcount needs against organizational strategy and roadmap
Build sophisticated financial and operational models that connect business drivers to staffing requirements, recruiting / vendor management plans, and budget implications
Build intuitive dashboards, metrics, and reports that highlight staffing utilization, labor productivity constraints, and capacity gaps
Partner with senior Operations and Finance leaders to develop scenarios balancing service levels, cost optimization, and growth objectives
Apply probabilistic modeling, Python-based simulation modeling, and artificial intelligence to simulate cost & efficiency trade-offs and resource optimization
Lead monthly headcount data analysis and vendor management strategy reviews to synthesize headcount performance inputs from multiple stakeholders into cohesive strategic recommendations
Analyze large, disparate datasets to uncover statistical trends in labor productivity and attrition
Monitor workforce KPIs and identify program gaps or execution issues that impact profitability and scalability
Improving data integrity and automating manual reporting workflows to increase functional efficiency

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in data science, management consulting, investment banking, engineering operations, FP&A, or strategic operations, ideally in a fast-scaling tech environment
Bachelor’s degree and / or work experience in a quantitative field (e.g. Operations Research, Business Analytics, Economics, Math, Statistics, Finance)
Exceptional Excel / Gsheets financial modeling skills, SQL, Python and statistical modeling skills and working with business intelligence tools (e.g., Mode, Tableau)
Experience building/maintaining data pipelines and DBT models
Strategic mindset with ability to balance detailed analysis with big-picture thinking
Track record of multi-functional leadership and excellent stakeholder management to drive rapid, effective execution across the organization
Strong executive presence with demonstrated ability to communicate complex analyses clearly to senior stakeholders
Superior attention to detail
Ownership mentality to drive issues and tasks to completion, with a strong bias for action

Support various mission areas by adapting to evolving operational priorities within a dynamic environment, ensuring mission success and operational readiness.
Maintain familiarity with classified environments such as the C2S Access Portal (CAP) and high-side AWS environments, ensuring compliance with security protocols.
Utilize knowledge of relational and non-relational databases, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, or DynamoDB, to support data-driven applications.

Summary

Positions to be filled are in various organizations at the following NASA Centers - Goddard Space Flight Center. NASA may fill positions in any of the following series and at any grade level listed in this announcement (GS-1301 and 1310 at the GS-11/12/13/14/15 levels).

Duties

Help

Document important results through technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, and presentations at relevant workshops and conferences.
Coordinate, plan, propose, execute, and evaluate projects supporting the overall objectives of NASA’s Earth Science Division and its partners.
Provide scientific and technical support or leadership in the development, interpretation, and use of remote sensing data products.
Develop and investigate new analytical techniques to advance the use of remote sensing data to understand the coupled Earth System.
Interact regularly with collaborating scientists and developers both within the organization and among the broader scientific and application communities to maximize cooperation and ensure compatibility with the organization’s scientific objectives.
Support or lead efforts to develop and implement new/enhanced methodological approaches and applications to study the physics and dynamics of the Earth System through a variety of remote sensing methods.
Support, develop, implement, and investigate state-of-the-art calibration and data quality assurance approaches for remote sensing systems and data products.
For supervisory positions, you will perform a full range of supervisory duties which includes assigning and evaluating work; recommending personnel actions; taking disciplinary actions; and identifying training needs and developing employees.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

This position is open to U.S. citizens, nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.
This position may require a one-year probationary/trial period. If selected, the requirement to serve such period will be determined by Title 5 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 11. **See Additional Information section**
You must meet qualifications requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Position subject to pre-employment background investigation or higher-level clearance. Investigation/Clearance may differ and be required based on the duty location/NASA Center requirements.
Financial Disclosure, Drug Testing, and/or the Travel Requirements for this position may differ and be required based on the duty location/NASA Center requirements.
For supervisory positions, a one-year supervisory probationary period may be required.
To be considered for employment, you must submit your complete application by 11:59 PM ET on August 21, 2026.

Qualifications

In addition to the Basic Education Requirement (in the Education section below), to qualify for this position you must meet the requirements below. Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work.

NASA utilizes OPM-approved qualification and rating requirements specific for Aerospace Technology (AST) positions which recognizes NASA's unique aerospace work. The specific qualifications and minimum education requirements are further described below and within the education section of the job announcement.

To qualify for GS-11, you must have:

You must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 level:
Working with others in a team environment to achieve goals set by team leads and/or supervisors;
Using methods developed by others to apply concepts, computing techniques, or methods in mathematics, physics, remote sensing, data science, or physical science to conduct guided research;
Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System.

OR

Completed all requirements for a doctoral degree (i.e., Ph.D. or equivalent) in an appropriate field

OR

Completed 3 full academic years of graduate education in an appropriate field

OR

Have an equivalent combination of experience and graduate study as discussed in a), b) and c) above

To qualify for GS-12, you must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level:

Working with others in a team environment to achieve goals set by team leads and/or supervisors;
Using methods developed by others to apply concepts, computing techniques, and methods in mathematics, physics, remote sensing, data science, or physical science to conduct research relevant to the Earth System;
Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

To qualify for GS-13, you must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level:

Working with others in a team environment to achieve goals set by team leads and/or supervisors;
Applying and adapting concepts, advanced computing techniques, and methods in mathematics, physics, remote sensing, data science, or physical science to conduct research and make predictions about the Earth System;
Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

To qualify for GS-14, you must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level:

Setting goals and leading others in a team environment to achieve them;
Applying concepts, advanced computing techniques, and methods in mathematics, physics, remote sensing, data science, or physical science to conduct research and make predictions about the coupled Earth System;
Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

To qualify for GS-15, you must have one year of directly related specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 level:

Taking leadership through building teams and ensuring they achieve the scientific goals;
Developing and advancing concepts, advanced computing techniques, and methods in mathematics, physics, remote sensing, data science, or physical science to conduct research and make predictions about the coupled Earth System;
Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

Your resume must include a clear and detailed narrative description, in your own words, of how you meet the required specialized experience. Experience statements copied from a position description, vacancy announcement or other reference material constitutes plagiarism and may result in disqualification and losing consideration for the job.

Please visit https://www.nasa.gov/careers/how-to-apply/#Artificial-Intelligence to review NASA's guidance on the use of artificial intelligent (AI) or AI-assisted tools during the application process.

Required college majors for applicants qualifying on the basis of graduate education only (GS-11)
:

702 Earth: Any appropriate field of engineering, physical or computer science or mathematics. Study must include or be supplemented by six semester hours (or the equivalent) in appropriate life or other natural science courses and include or be supplemented by at least two courses which would provide knowledge of subjects appropriate to the vacancy being filled.

730 Measurement: Aeronautical Engineering, Aeronautics, Aerospace Engineering, Astronautical Engineering, Astronautics, Astronomy, Astrophysics, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering (except power), Electronics Engineering, Applied Mechanics, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, Nuclear Engineering, Nuclear Engineering Physics, Oceanography, Optical Engineering. Promotion Potential:

Education

Basic Education Requirement:

You must have successfully completed a bachelor's degree with a major in one of the following:

Engineering from a college or university that has ABET accredited engineering programs
Physical Science, Mathematics, Life Science or other field of Science
Computer Science that included 30 semester hours or 45 quarter hours of course work in any combination of mathematics, statistics and computer science with at least half of those hours in mathematics and statistics courses that included differential and integral calculus; and that provided an in-depth knowledge of theoretical and practical applications of computer science, including digital computer system architecture and system software organization, the representation and transformation of information structures, and the theoretical models for such representations and transformations.

Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

Using remote sensing data and/or applied science techniques to understand and characterize the interactions among the elements of the Earth System in general.

LMI is seeking a Capability Development Program Coordinator
to support a Special Operations Command (SOCOM) mission partner with requirements development, capability-gap analysis, system integration, equipment modernization, testing, procurement planning, material fielding, and life-cycle replacement activities. The Program Coordinator will serve as a subject matter expert for assigned Soldier capability programs and help translate operational needs into executable equipment and technology solutions aligned with mission requirements, resources, schedules, and approved acquisition objectives.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and achieve mission success.

This position requires an active Secret security clearance.

Responsibilities

Support the development, analysis, validation, documentation, staffing, and maintenance of operational requirements for new and modernized Soldier capabilities.
Identify and define equipment needs by engaging operational users, leaders, capability developers, acquisition professionals, testers, logisticians, and other mission stakeholders.
Analyze capability gaps and assess potential materiel and non-materiel solutions against operational effectiveness, technical feasibility, interoperability, cost, schedule, sustainment, and life-cycle considerations.
Develop and maintain life-cycle replacement plans, technology-refresh strategies, modernization roadmaps, and investment recommendations for assigned equipment portfolios.
Guide capability initiatives and assigned programs through applicable review, validation, approval, resourcing, acquisition, integration, testing, and fielding processes.
Prepare decision-support products, requirements documents, executive briefings, cost and schedule analyses, risk assessments, courses of action, and program-status reports for senior leaders.
Advise leaders on technology-upgrade plans and investment priorities for emerging combat capabilities.
Coordinate with Army, special operations, acquisition, testing, logistics, training, cybersecurity, communications, and other military offices to ensure systems are integrated, interoperable, supportable, and aligned with mission requirements.
Serve as the subject matter expert for assigned capability programs and Programs of Record.
Plan, coordinate, oversee, and assess developmental tests, operational tests, user assessments, demonstrations, experimentation events, and field evaluations.
Develop test objectives, user scenarios, evaluation criteria, schedules, risk controls, data-collection plans, and after-action products in coordination with government and technical stakeholders.
Translate approved procurement objectives into executable equipment-purchasing plans, acquisition schedules, delivery priorities, and funding requirements.
Develop and coordinate material fielding plans that address equipment allocation, accountability, transportation, facilities, training, technical documentation, sustainment, and user acceptance.
Monitor program cost, schedule, performance, risk, integration, procurement, testing, fielding, and sustainment activities; identify issues and recommend corrective actions.
Respond to requests for information from SOCOM and Army stakeholders regarding current and future technologies, assigned capability portfolios, and Programs of Record.
Conduct market research and technology assessments to identify commercial, government, and emerging solutions with potential application to special operations missions.
Maintain program records, requirements traceability, decision logs, risk registers, schedules, fielding trackers, configuration information, and other program-management products.
Coordinate across operational commands, headquarters staff sections, program offices, laboratories, test organizations, industry partners, and supported units to synchronize capability development and delivery.

Active Secret security clearance.
Minimum of eight years of experience supporting Department of War capability development, requirements analysis, acquisition, program management, systems integration, testing, equipment fielding, or life-cycle management activities.
Experience supporting U.S. Special Operations Forces, a Special Operations Command organization, or another operationally focused Department of War mission partner.
Demonstrated experience identifying operational capability gaps and translating user needs into documented equipment, system, or technology requirements.
Experience assessing potential solutions based on operational utility, technical performance, integration, interoperability, cost, schedule, sustainment, and risk.
Experience supporting requirements, acquisition, integration, test and evaluation, procurement, material fielding, or life-cycle replacement processes for military equipment.
Experience serving as a subject matter expert or program integrator for assigned capabilities, equipment portfolios, or Programs of Record.
Ability to develop and present executive briefings, decision papers, cost and schedule analyses, risk assessments, procurement plans, fielding plans, and program-status products.
Ability to coordinate effectively across operational users, senior leaders, acquisition personnel, engineers, logisticians, testers, resource managers, technical teams, and industry partners.
Strong analytical, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Teams, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Project, and SharePoint.
Ability to independently manage multiple concurrent programs, requirements, stakeholder actions, and deadlines in a high-tempo environment.
Ability to travel periodically in support of testing, assessments, demonstrations, fielding activities, and stakeholder engagements.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, systems engineering, program management, business administration, logistics, acquisition management, military studies, or a related discipline.
Prior military service within U.S. Special Operations Forces or another operationally focused Army organization.
Experience supporting a G-3, G-8, force-modernization organization, capability-development office, program executive office, program management office, or Army Futures Command organization.
